name: Fluconazole
route_note: oral capsules, tablets or suspension once daily (single dose for vaginal candidiasis); IV infusion
originator: Pfizer (Ken Richardson and colleagues, Sandwich, UK)

discovery.by: Ken Richardson and colleagues, Pfizer UK
discovery.note: Water-soluble bis-triazole designed for good oral absorption, metabolic stability and penetration into cerebrospinal fluid.

rx_status: prescription; single-dose vaginal thrush capsule OTC in some countries
tagline: Well-absorbed triazole for candidiasis and cryptococcal meningitis
summary: Fluconazole is a triazole antifungal that is almost completely absorbed orally and penetrates well into body fluids including cerebrospinal fluid. It is a mainstay for Candida infections, from vaginal thrush to candidaemia, and for cryptococcal meningitis, especially in people with HIV. It has no useful activity against moulds such as Aspergillus.
mechanism: Azoles inhibit lanosterol 14α-demethylase (CYP51, encoded by ERG11 in yeasts and cyp51A in Aspergillus), a fungal cytochrome P450 enzyme needed to make ergosterol, the main sterol of fungal cell membranes. Ergosterol depletion and accumulation of toxic 14α-methylated sterols disrupt membrane structure and the function of membrane-bound enzymes, stopping fungal growth.

Fluconazole is fungistatic against most Candida species. Candida krusei is intrinsically resistant, C. glabrata is often less susceptible, and resistance in C. albicans and Candida auris involves ERG11 mutations and efflux pumps (CDR1, MDR1).
uses: Candidaemia and other invasive Candida infections
Cryptococcal meningitis (with amphotericin B/flucytosine induction and as consolidation and maintenance)
Antifungal prophylaxis in bone-marrow transplantation and other high-risk patients

history.title: Discovery
history.detail: Pfizer chemists in Sandwich, UK, identify fluconazole.

history.title: First approval
history.detail: Fluconazole is approved in the UK.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Diflucan is approved in the US in January 1990 and becomes widely used for AIDS-related cryptococcal meningitis and candidiasis.

history.title: Single-dose vaginal therapy
history.detail: A single 150 mg oral dose is approved for vaginal candidiasis.

history.title: US generics
history.detail: Generic fluconazole becomes available in the US.

history.title: Candida auris
history.detail: Health agencies warn about Candida auris, a multidrug-resistant yeast usually resistant to fluconazole.

pk.metabolism: minimal hepatic metabolism; inhibits CYP2C9, CYP2C19 and CYP3A4

serious: QT prolongation and torsades de pointes
possible birth defects with high-dose prolonged use in early pregnancy

facts: Fluconazole reaches cerebrospinal fluid concentrations of about 70–80% of plasma levels.
Pfizer's donation programme, starting in 2000, supplied fluconazole free for HIV-related cryptococcal meningitis in many low-income countries.
